subject: science
passage: Since the 1960s, the Dead Sea has been shrinking as the rivers that feed it are diverted for farms and cities, and its surface now drops by about a meter a year. As the shoreline retreats, fresh groundwater flows into layers of salt left behind by the lake, dissolving them and opening cavities that collapse without warning. Thousands of sinkholes have appeared, swallowing sections of highway and a stretch of beach. Local councils have put a blunt question to the engineers monitoring the area: can the remaining roads be kept open at ______ answers have been cautious, since no one can predict where the next collapse will occur.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Can the remaining roads be kept open at all" is a direct question, quoted as the councils put it, so it must end with a question mark. The next sentence, "The answers have been cautious," then begins with a capital letter.
explanation.A: Correct. A question mark ends the direct question, and "The answers …" begins a new sentence.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A comma cannot end the question, and joining it to the next independent clause with a comma alone creates a comma splice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the question runs straight into the next sentence, and "at all the answers" cannot be read clearly.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A period cannot end a direct question; "can the remaining roads be kept open at all" asks something, so it needs a question mark.
